title: Electromagnetically Consistent Federated RIS Channel Estimation with Component-Level Full-Wave Validation
content: Learned reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) channel estimators are typically evaluated on an idealized diagonal phase-shift surface, with noise added directly to the channel and observations spaced by a nominal slot. This paper removes those idealizations and quantifies which conclusions persist. We build an electromagnetically consistent RIS generator (varactor-loaded cell, multiple-scattering mutual coupling, spherical wavefronts), validated at component level against full-wave simulation, and drive it with a true M+1 pilot sweep and cascaded least squares under non-Markovian Jakes dynamics; a federated long shortterm memory estimator competes against classical sequence filters, including a deployable Kalman filter. Two idealizations favour learning, silently and in the same direction. Referring the unit-cell reflection to the wave impedance instead of the element self-impedance models the passive surface as active, inflating the dipole-kernel coupling penalty 96-fold for least squares against 2.9-fold for the learned estimator; spacing observations by one slot instead of the full sweep overstates temporal correlation, and correcting it costs the recurrent estimators 40 to 45%. Both are numerically silent, and both audits incur negligible overhead. Under the corrected models the deployable Kalman filter leads at every SNR, and a tenfold per-column channel-NMSE lead delivers 0.36 to 0.47 dB less field at the user in scene-paired tests. An origin-blind playoff selects hand-tuned hyperparameters over the multi-objective search. A coherence budget separates feasible operating points from stress tests. These conclusions hold for the full-sweep acquisition, mixed- SNR training and characterized unit-cell family investigated. Channel NMSE misranks the estimators against the delivered field.
